title: Release Artifacts Manifest
description: Declarative, single-source-of-truth list of every binary/file that must ship in a release cargo. One manifest replaces N scattered `test -s <path>` checks hand-added to a release workflow each time a missing artifact causes an outage.

$schemaVersion.description: Manifest schema version, for forward-compatible parsing.

id.description: Stable identifier for this artifact, used in verify/imprint reports. Matches the binary's canonical name where practical (e.g. pd-bosun).

sourcePath.description: Where the build step produces this artifact (relative to repo root, or absolute). Optional -- some artifacts are staged directly by the build step and never read back from sourcePath.

stagedPath.description: Where the artifact must exist in the sealed release cargo (the directory that gets tarred/zipped/uploaded). This is the path `verify` checks -- it is the contract with the installer, not with the build step.

required.description: If true, a missing artifact fails the release (fail-loud). If false, absence is recorded as SKIP, not FAIL -- for genuinely optional/platform-conditional artifacts.

executable.description: If true, verify also checks the file has at least one execute bit set (chmod +x was not silently dropped by an archive/copy step).

minBytes.description: Minimum acceptable file size. Catches truncated uploads, zero-byte placeholder files, and empty-stub builds -- not just total absence. Set close to (but below) the artifact's known real size; do not leave at the default 1 for anything that has ever shipped empty.

description.description: One line: what this artifact is and why it must ship. Shows up in verify failure output so the person reading CI logs knows the blast radius, not just a path.
